summary: Intermittent rerank tail-latency and nondeterministic scores after embedding cache TTL expiry triggers CPU fallback
description: Issue summary: FocusText.ai reports recurring spikes in rerank tail latency (~500-1200ms) and nondeterministic top-k ordering for a subset of requests. Spikes correlate with embedding cache TTL expirations which cause synchronous refetch + reranker CPU fallback. Impact: user-facing search ranking instability and increased P95/P99 latency. Environment: Dedicated customer pool in us-east, embedding cache is Redis cluster with per-namespace TTL. Temporal pattern: spikes appear when cache misses spike after periodic namespace TTL sweeps or backfills.
impact: Search API P95 increased from 120ms to 700-1200ms for ~2-5% of requests during cache churn windows; reported customer-facing ranking changes and occasional 503s from the reranker with traceback referencing CPU fallback path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer dataset and send sustained 500 req/s embedding+rerank workload against dedicated pool in us-east
2) Set embedding cache TTL artificially low (simulate rolling TTL expiry) or trigger namespace backfill to induce mass cache misses
3) Observe reranker latency and top-k ordering for requests that miss cache vs warm requests
4) Capture logs from proxy, cache, and reranker services during TTL expiry window
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z reranker ERROR cpu_fallback_path.cpp:142 - fallback due to missing GPU kvcache, processing in FP32 CPU mode, request_id=aa3f4b
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z cache INFO redis: cache_miss namespace=focustext:docs key=embed:12345
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z proxy WARN proxy_manager: queue_growth - client_qsize=80, worker_qsize=0, backpressure=true
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Mass cache-miss events force synchronous embed recompute which then routes to GPU but falls back to CPU when kv cache unavailable leading to slower FP32 code path and nondet floating point ordering.

Hypothesis B: Embedding variant mismatch between cached vectors (embedder-v1-1536) and live model (embedder-v2-1024) triggers additional normalization path that runs on CPU. We found a small number of stale cache entries with legacy shape headers in redis during incident window.
Checked dashboards: saw correlated spikes on redis eviction rate and reranker.cpu_util; GPU nodes reported transient kv-cache connection errors (logs reference transient gRPC timeouts to kv-store).

Reproduced locally by expiring cache namespace and instrumenting reranker: observed FP32 path uses a different normalization routine which produces slight cosine differences leading to top-k order changes for near-tie candidates.

Related PR discovered that changed embedder alias routing two weeks ago: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/128 - it introduced alias fallback logic that may populate legacy-shaped embeddings into cache during a rollout.
Customer workload patterns: periodic nightly backfills from FocusText.ai coincide with the cache-sweep windows and increase miss storms.
comments: Support (Asha): Initial triage with customer and asked for request ids and a short reproduction script. Customer provided sample request ids and their nightly backfill schedule.
SRE (Diego): Noted redis eviction burst and temporary gRPC kv-store timeouts between 14:11 and 14:15. Adding temporary autoscale to cache replicas for mitigation.

Research (Elena): Confirmed normalization code path difference between CPU fallback and GPU path can change score ordering for near-ties; wrote quick unit test demonstrating nondeterministic top-k when switching FP paths.
Customer (FocusText.ai - Ben): Able to throttle backfills which reduces frequency of spikes; requests a long-term fix and SLA credit investigation.
Eng (Marco): Working on hotfix to avoid running CPU normalization for embed sizes we don't support and to enforce strict dimension validation on cache write/read.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased cache replica count and adjusted eviction thresholds for the customer's namespace to reduce TTL churn. 2) Added temporary rate limiter on backfill ingestion for dedicated pools. 3) Deployed hotfix to router to reject writing legacy-shaped embeddings into active cache namespaces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/140). 4) Added defensive check in reranker to prefer GPU normalization path or defer request with 429 to upstream when fallback would cause nondet scoring. Follow-ups: schedule permanent fix to normalization convergence on CPU/GPU parity, add alerting for cache-shape-mismatch, and prepare SLA credit proposal for customer. Currently status: mitigation live; working on code fix and permanent tests.
